title: Testing Whether Theoretical Corrigibility Definitions Are Empirically Distinguishable

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Clarifies whether multiple corrigibility definitions are empirically equivalent. If they are distinguishable, the field can compare them empirically; if not, theoretical distinctions are less important. Either result is valuable for prioritizing alignment research directions.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Simple RL agents with three different reward objectives in a toy environment. Standard RL libraries handle this well. Designing the 50-scenario test suite requires thought but no advanced technical skills. Medium compute is more than sufficient.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three training objectives and 50 test scenarios. Each training objective is a separate RL run, but in toy environments these are fast. The main scope concern is designing 50 meaningful scenarios. Could narrow to 20 scenarios.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
